text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The international mediator for the sucession of former Yugoslav federation assets, Sir Arthur Watts, said there was broad agreement on the principles but not on the actual division of assets. He said the most difficult issue would be defining state assets.

- The Bosnian presidency on Thursday did not agree on how to distribute of diplomatic posts because Croat officials insist on an ethnic balance based on the constitution. The Moslems insist that the division should be based on the pre-war 1991 census, says foreign minister Jadranko Prlic.
- McDonald's might open a restaurant in Sarajevo within a year and a half, depending on market conditions, says Hasan Muratovic, foreign trade minister, after meeting with McDonald's delegation.

- The Council of Ministers session on Thursday focused on the forthcoming donors' conference in Brussels and the composition of the Bosnian delegation. Serb co-chairman, Boro Bosic, refused to attend the meeting because he said NATO could not be trusted to provide security for his staff in Sarajevo.

- The Moslem chairman of the collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, has been invited by Iran to attend the next summit of Islamic countries even though Bosnia is not a member of the Organisation of Islamic Countries.
- The number of requests for issuing Bosnian passports to citizens of the Serb entity in Bosnia has increased, interior ministry says.
- The French justice ministry requested the extradition of the two Frenchmen recently sentenced to twenty years each for a series of armed robberies in which two people died.

- The Bosnian presidency will consider a proposal on establishing diplomatic relations with neighbouring Yugoslavia without conditions, in accordance with the declaration from major powers issued recently in Sintra, Portugal.

- The International Organisation for Threatened Peoples called on former High Represenative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt, to reveal publicly the agreement which he allegedly reached during secret talks with Bosnian Serb General Ratko Mladic and Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic regarding the Srebrenica enclave. --Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
